data.title: Ed Morse Says Current Conditions Are Inflationary
data.description: Ed Morse, senior advisor and commodities strategist at Hartree Partners, said the current environment is inflationary. He joined Tome Keene on “Bloomberg Money” to discuss the oil market, his career and China, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Bill Ackman Reacts to Jensen Huang's Nvidia Exit, Praises Anthropic IPO Roadshow Presentation
data.description: Pershing Square founder and CEO Bill Ackman said it was sad to see Jensen Huang leave Nvidia and that Huang would go on to do something great, according to Bloomberg. Ackman also said he was impressed by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's presentation at the company's IPO roadshow event in New York.

data.title: Bitcoin’s Billion-Dollar Wipeouts Are Becoming More Familiar
data.description: Bitcoin traders are accustomed to sharp market swings that can decimate portfolios within minutes. According to Bloomberg, the wipeouts are becoming bigger and more frequent, even by crypto standards.

data.title: STOCKS | Barclays Desk Turns Tactically Bullish on US Equities for First Time Since Mid-March
data.description: Barclays’ trading desk has turned tactically bullish on US equities for the first time since mid-March, as a sharp pullback in investor positioning and easing volatility pressures created an attractive opportunity for a tactical rebound, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Grizzlies vs. Pelicans Market: Cameron Boozer Points Yes Probability Rises 20 Points
data.description: On Polymarket’s “Grizzlies vs. Pelicans” market, the “Yes” probability for “Cameron Boozer: Points O/U 17.5” rose to 49.5% from 29.5% one hour earlier, a 20-percentage-point increase. According to ChainCatcher, the probability experienced a sharp fluctuation.

data.title: Nakamoto Sold 184 BTC in Q3 and Now Holds 4,283 BTC
data.description: Nakamoto, owned by David Bailey, sold 184 bitcoin in the third quarter and currently holds 4,283 bitcoin. According to Odaily, Bitcoin Treasuries said in a post on X that Nakamoto ranks 21st on its Bitcoin Top 100 list.

data.title: Nvidia Board Is Selecting CEO Search Firms, Says No Candidates Have Been Contacted
data.description: Nvidia's board said it is selecting executive search firms to begin recruiting for the CEO position. According to Sina Finance, the board said it has not formally contacted any potential candidates and called speculation about specific internal or external candidates premature.

data.title: Nvidia Has Not Selected Search Firm for Permanent Huang Successor
data.description: According to CNBC, Nvidia’s board said it has not selected a search firm to identify a permanent successor to former CEO Jensen Huang. The board is in the process of selecting a firm and has not formally engaged any potential candidates.

data.title: STOCKS | House Democrats to Investigate Nvidia Scandal and National Security Implications
data.description: On November 14, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries said House Democrats would conduct an in-depth investigation into Nvidia’s recent scandal and its possible national security implications. According to Sina Finance, Jeffries said at an event in Denver on Friday that Democratic Representative Jim Himes and the House Intelligence Committee would lead the investigation. The personal scandal involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang continued to unfold, while U.S. Commerce Secretary Lutnick’s role in chip policy also came under scrutiny.

data.title: AI TRENDS | Injective Launches Anthropic Pre-IPO Market Ahead of Nasdaq Listing
data.description: Injective has launched a pre-IPO market for Anthropic ahead of the company’s Nasdaq listing. According to Odaily, Injective said on X that users can participate in the market with one click.

data.title: Howard Lutnick Faces Scrutiny Over Cantor Fitzgerald’s Nvidia Ties
data.description:
According to CNBC, Cantor Fitzgerald, the firm formerly run by Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and now led by his sons, reported a 49% decline in its Nvidia shareholding between September 2025 and March 2026, while continuing to arrange financing for companies in Nvidia’s business network. Cantor’s reported Nvidia holdings fell from 3 million shares in December to 1.78 million by the end of March, but the filings do not show why the firm reduced its reported position or whether its overall financial exposure declined. The firm said its reported holdings reflected client swap transactions and that it had only immaterial stand-alone proprietary positions in Nvidia.

The scrutiny follows reports that Lutnick resisted efforts to restrict Singapore-based Megaspeed, which was suspected of funneling Nvidia chips to China, despite intelligence concerns involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Cantor was one of seven bookrunners on IREN’s $3 billion convertible bond offering, which closed in May; Nvidia and IREN had announced a five-year, $3.4 billion cloud-computing contract and a strategic partnership. There is no evidence that Lutnick’s sons had advance knowledge of the intelligence concerns, that Cantor’s reported holdings changes were tied to warnings, or that the firm’s business interests influenced Lutnick’s decisions. Former White House ethics lawyer Richard Painter said the relationship could create an appearance of concern, while noting there was no proof Lutnick shared nonpublic information with Cantor.

data.title: Supreme Court to Hear Robinhood Bid to Toss IPO Disclosure Lawsuit
data.description: According to CNBC, the Supreme Court on Friday agreed to consider Robinhood’s effort to block an investor lawsuit alleging the company omitted interim financial data from its 2021 initial public offering. The case challenges a 9th Circuit U.S. Court of Appeals ruling that revived the lawsuit, which a San Francisco federal judge had previously dismissed. The Trump administration urged the Supreme Court to hear Robinhood’s appeal.

data.title: Goldman Sachs Seeks Two Revenue Streams From Anthropic IPO as Morgan Stanley and Rivals Compete
data.description:
According to CNBC, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are co-leading Anthropic’s IPO, which could raise $64.35 billion, and Goldman aims to earn underwriting fees while pursuing wealth-management clients among the company’s founders, executives and employees. The offering is expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq next Thursday. Evercore ISI analyst Glenn Schorr estimated total underwriting fees of roughly $395 million; under his base-case scenario, Goldman and Morgan Stanley could each receive about $79 million.

JPMorgan, Citigroup and Bank of America are also underwriters and have wealth-management businesses. Morgan Stanley attracted a record $232 billion in net new assets in the third quarter, with IPO-related flows accounting for just over half of the total. A Goldman spokesperson said the firm sees wealth planning as an extension of its advisory relationships with executives involved in IPOs, financing or M&A transactions.

data.title: AI | Dario Amodei Says Anthropic Is Working to Prevent AI Agents From Running Unchecked
data.description: Anthropic CEO and co-founder Dario Amodei said the company is continuously working on “safety and security and alignment” and does not want AI agents to “run wild,” according to Bloomberg. He spoke Friday during a livestreamed conversation with JPMorgan Chase Chairman and CEO Jamie Dimon as part of Anthropic’s IPO roadshow.

data.title: LlamaRisk Proposes Dynamic Borrowing Caps for Aave V3
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, LlamaRisk proposed introducing dynamic borrowing caps for Aave V3. Chainlink CRE would calculate cap increases to limit the pace of borrowing growth.

data.title: Jim Cramer: Higher Yields Weigh on Stocks as Club Trims TJX, Adds Kimberly-Clark and Constellation Brands
data.description: According to CNBC, Jim Cramer said higher bond yields were weighing on stocks. The Nasdaq fell more than 1% Friday, extending its declines to a second straight session. The club trimmed TJX ahead of next week’s earnings and used the proceeds to add to Kimberly-Clark and Constellation Brands, its newest portfolio position. Cramer called Friday’s drop in Advanced Micro Devices a buying opportunity and said he would start a position in AMD and exit Intel if unrestricted.

data.title: Canada Puts $140 Million Into LNG Project Backed by Indonesia’s Richest Person
data.description: Canada’s government injected C$200 million ($140 million) into a west coast liquefied natural gas project backed by Indonesia’s richest person, according to Bloomberg. Prime Minister Mark Carney is pushing to diversify exports away from the US.

data.title: STOCKS | Barclays Reportedly Plans to Cut About 200 Investment Banking Jobs Starting Next Week After Announcing 5,000 Job Cuts
data.description: Barclays plans to begin another round of layoffs as early as next Tuesday, cutting about 200 jobs in its investment banking division, mainly in New York and London, across seniority levels. According to Sina Finance, people familiar with the matter said the cuts follow the bank’s announcement last month of plans to eliminate about 5,000 positions. One source said the latest reductions are part of Barclays’ annual operational efficiency plan, intended to optimize staffing and direct more resources to priority businesses and talent areas. A Barclays spokesperson declined to comment.

data.title: Amazon’s First North American Logistics Union Contract Set in Canada
data.description: An independent arbitrator imposed terms Friday for a union contract covering about 700 Amazon.com Inc. warehouse employees in western Canada, making them the company’s first North American logistics workers covered by such an agreement, Bloomberg reported, citing a person familiar with the matter. Unifor, one of the nation’s largest private-sector unions, is party to the contract.

data.title: San Francisco Fed President Mary C. Daly: FOMC Must Remain Transparent and Accountable
data.description: According to Jin10, San Francisco Fed President Mary C. Daly said the FOMC must remain transparent and accountable and communicate policy clearly.
